c.tagline: A lakeside town of ancient churches on one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are cheap and metered but confirm the fare or that the meter is on before setting off; there is no Uber, so use ranks or phone a local taxi company.

emergency.note: 112 is the general European emergency number; it reaches police, fire and ambulance from any phone.

hood_landmark.Kaneo: Church of St John at Kaneo Ohrid
hood_landmark.Centar: Ohrid town centre Sveti Kliment square

avoid.reason: Agree taxi fares in advance and watch belongings on the crowded summer boardwalk; otherwise usual awareness.

hood_desc: The steep, cobbled UNESCO core rising from the lake through medieval churches, the ancient theatre and Samuel's Fortress; a maze of stone houses, konaks and viewpoints — the essential place to stay for sights and atmosphere.

The tranquil lakeside neighborhood below the Old Town, famous for the cliff-top Church of St John at Kaneo and its little swimming beach shaded by olive trees; serene and scenic, ideal for a romantic, restful stay.
The waterfront promenade of Kej strung with restaurants, cafes, bars and boat docks; the sociable, animated heart of the lakefront where the town comes out to stroll each evening.
The modern town center just back from the water around the main square and Sveti Kliment, with markets, shops, the bus station and everyday local life; the practical, convenient base.

The string of southern lakeshore resorts and beaches — Sveti Stefan, Lagadin and beyond toward the monastery of St Naum — lined with hotels and pebbly swimming coves; a quiet, holiday base on the water outside town.

water.note: Tap water is spring-fed and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Limited daytime service; buses are infrequent and stop running in the evening, so most visitors walk or take taxis.
transit.note: Ohrid has no metro or tram and only a sparse local bus service; the compact center is best walked, with cheap taxis and intercity buses (to Skopje, Bitola and Struga) filling the gaps.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (denars) on board; there is no smart-card or app ticketing. Taxis are metered and inexpensive.

landmarks: Church of St. John at Kaneo
Perched on a cliff above Lake Ohrid's turquoise water, this thirteenth-century Byzantine church is Macedonia's most photographed sight.
Samuel's Fortress
The mighty ramparts of Tsar Samuel's tenth-century Bulgarian capital crown Ohrid's hill with sweeping views over lake, town and mountains.
Ancient Theatre of Ohrid
A Hellenistic amphitheater from 200 BC, rediscovered by chance, now staging summer festival performances above the old town's rooftops.
Church of St. Sophia
Ohrid's medieval cathedral preserves some of the Balkans' finest eleventh-century Byzantine frescoes beneath its austere brick arcades.
Plaošnik (Church of Sts. Clement and Panteleimon)
The restored monastery where St. Clement founded Europe's first Slavic university around 893, cradle of the Cyrillic literary tradition.
Monastery of Saint Naum
A cliff-top monastery near the Albanian border, ringed by peacocks and crystal springs, reachable by a glorious boat ride down the lake.
Old Bazaar and Čaršija
Ohrid's cobbled market street climbs from the harbor plane tree past pearl workshops, cafés and Ottoman-era houses toward the upper gate.
Bay of Bones Museum
A reconstructed Bronze Age pile-dwelling settlement stands on stilts over the lake, an evocative open-air museum on the Gradište peninsula.
Robevi Family House (National Museum)
A magnificent nineteenth-century Ohrid mansion of carved wooden ceilings, housing archaeological treasures and showcasing the town's celebrated domestic architecture.
Lake Ohrid Boardwalk and Potpeš Beach
A wooden walkway hugs the cliffs from Kaneo to pebble coves, delivering swimmers and strollers the lake's dreamiest sunset views.

train.note: No railway has ever reached Ohrid: the line from Skopje ends at Kicevo about 60 km north, and the alternative railhead is Bitola roughly 80 km southeast, with buses covering the last stretch. Both are worked by Makedonski Zeleznici Transport (https://mzt.mk/) and are infrequent - Kicevo has at times had a single train a day. On the Albanian side the railway to Pogradec closed in 2012 and has not reopened. International services from North Macedonia are limited to an unreliable Skopje-Pristina train; the Belgrade and Thessaloniki links are dormant and the Skopje-Sofia line is not expected before 2027.

bus.note: Intercity buses from Ohrid's station run to Skopje (~3 hr), Bitola, Struga and Skopje International Airport; cross-border services reach Tirana and the Albanian side of the lake, mostly in the warmer months. The station is about 2 km from the old town, a short taxi or local bus ride away. Skopje departures are roughly hourly from around 830 denars, and tickets are bought in cash at the counter windows rather than online. Both North Macedonia and Albania are outside Schengen, so passports are checked and stamped at Qafe Thane, and the Tirana run takes four to five hours including formalities.

intl.to: Pogradec (Albania) - daily boat across Lake Ohrid in the tourist season, leaving Ohrid around 10:00
intl.op: local Lake Ohrid boat operators, tickets at the quay

intl.to: Sveti Naum (North Macedonia) - ~1 hr 30 min lake boat along the southern shore
intl.op: local Lake Ohrid boat operators, tickets at the quay

ferry.note: Boats leave from the quay on Ohrid's lakefront, two minutes from the old town, and are run by small local operators who sell tickets on the spot rather than online. The scenic run south to the Sveti Naum monastery near the Albanian border takes about an hour and a half each way and is the most popular trip, often combined with a bus back. The cross-border service to Pogradec in Albania sails in the tourist season only, leaving around 10:00. Almost nothing runs in winter, when the lake gets rough and demand disappears; if you take the Albanian boat, make sure your passport is stamped before you sail.

half.name: Monastery of St Naum
half.blurb: A 10th-century lakeside monastery with peacocks and the crystal springs of the Black Drin, ~29 km south along the lake.

half.name: Struga
half.blurb: The relaxed lakeside town where the Black Drin flows out of Lake Ohrid, known for its poetry festival, ~15 km away.

full.name: Galičica National Park & Lake Prespa
full.blurb: A mountain drive over Galičica between Lakes Ohrid and Prespa, with panoramic viewpoints.

full.name: Bitola & Heraclea Lyncestis
full.blurb: Elegant consular-era Bitola and the Roman ruins of Heraclea with fine mosaics, ~1.5 hr east.

full.name: Skopje
full.blurb: The eclectic national capital, about three hours away, with its old bazaar and monumental center.
